If we're doing a rename, I think we should use the generic term [file manager](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File_manager). Finder/Files are specific application names.
Essentially, this would mean wrapping each `.on_action` or `.action` with something like `.when(cfg!(target_os = "OPERATING SYSTEM"), |this| { this.action(/*....*/) })`
@mikayla-maki wrapped actions with your suggestion. Check it if it is enough. Thank you.
This pr can be merged or I have to solve conflicts first?

> This pr can be merged or I have to solve conflicts first?

I think rebasing on main (or merging it in) and fixing the conflicts would be great.
@mrnugget done it. so we can merge?
I don't have a mac can anyone test before merging?

I tested on Linux and on macOS. On Linux everything works as expected. On macOS the action is now called "Reveal in File Manager".

I think @mikayla-maki's idea was that we define two actions: `RevealInFinder` and `RevealInFileManager` and only use one of two, depending on the target dir. (Also: `reveal_in_finder` is still the method name.)

The problem is that for the `vim.json` keybindings we have to pick one over the other and we can't do a runtime check of `vim.enabled` to define one or the other action.

Sooooo, should we go with the rename then, @mikayla-maki? :D

I have observed that the context menu contains both 'Trash' and 'Delete' options. Based on the platform, we can display only one option. 

I'm checking what the solutions are.

> I have observed that the context menu contains both 'Trash' and 'Delete' options. Based on the platform, we can display only one option.
> 
> I'm checking what the solutions are.

Don't all major desktop platforms (Linux, MacOS, Windows) have both delete and trash?

@someone13574 Yes all the platform supports both trash and delete but the interpretation is different in each one:
Mac:
Trash (Command + Delete) -> Soft delete
Delete (Option + Command + Delete)-> Hard delete

Windows:
Recycle Bin (Delete) -> Soft delete
Delete (Ctrl + Shift + Delete) -> Hard delete

I have used the linux but don't have exact idea.
@dhairyanadapara But that’s just a keybinding change. Your first comment was about not showing options.

Hey @someone13574, I realized I misunderstood the code and mistakenly suggested its removal. I've checked again, and everything works as expected. However, we should update the copy text for "Trash" and "Delete" to help users differentiate between them more easily. The confusion might have arisen because both "Delete" and "Trash" are shown. Typically, applications only display "Trash" or a soft delete option. If users want to permanently delete something, they can use the keybinding or the file explorer.
